claims.statement: Every skill in the repo is governed by one shared model that answers three questions: how much must be read to use it (progressive disclosure), what an agent must do to run it (portability constraint), and what a skill may/may not require of the host harness (no-extra-tools invariant). The references/ directory is the authoritative detail layer beneath SKILL.md.

A skill is consumed in three unequal layers: (1) YAML frontmatter name+description as the registration/discovery layer, (2) the full SKILL.md body as a short control plane, (3) the references/ directory as the authoritative detail layer. The control plane must list/describe progressively, observe when needed, follow next pointers, require the already-open browser, and obtain exact plan approval for writes — and must NOT enumerate the whole registry or teach Playwright, bundling, or selectors.

The portability constraint is the single most important invariant: an agent only needs to read SKILL.md, use local files, and start a local process. A generated skill can be copied to any skill location understood by an agent; local process execution is sufficient. The runtime dependency floor is Node >=22.16 plus the pinned playwright-cli on PATH; no npm install is needed for normal use.

The no-extra-tools invariant constrains what may be added to a skill: a generated skill requires no harness-specific tools, MCP, plugins, SDKs, or special agent permissions. Specifically, no agents/openai.yaml, custom tool definitions, MCP configs, harness SDKs, or harness permissions are necessary. Any addition that would make a skill depend on a particular agent's tool set is disallowed.

The SKILL.md frontmatter contract is defined by the builder's template SKILL.template.md: it carries exactly two fields — name (the skill's stable slug, e.g. cardmarket-automation) and description (a one-line summary, with a BUILD_REQUIRED marker when unconfigured). No other identity metadata is required; all behavioral content lives in the body and references.

The required reference-directory layout is: SKILL.md, scripts/site-runtime.mjs (compiled Node entry point), runtime/manifest.json, runtime/actions/*.js (precompiled domain + observation bundles), src/ (pages/, components/, actions/, runtime/, build.ts, validate-build.ts), site.config.ts, package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, and references/ (actions.md, flows.md, selectors.md, verification.md, build-state.json). The runtime is precompiled so normal use needs neither node_modules nor src/; bundles are generated artifacts and must never be hand-edited.

The cardmarket-automation SKILL.md declares name: cardmarket-automation and a description summarizing guarded Cardmarket state-machine automation (login state, search, detail, sellers, versions, artworks, own offers, approved offer updates) that attaches to an existing Chrome session. Its references/ directory contains actions.md (full parameter and output schemas), flows.md, selectors.md, verification.md, and build-state.json.

The distribution rules: build with npm install/ci, npm run build, npm run verify; ship the compiled scripts/ and runtime/ so list/describe and normal actions run without node_modules or src/; keep src/ in the full handoff for repair. The scaffold starts intentionally unconfigured; --demo overlays a deterministic local inventory fixture with two example actions and a static localhost server and is a test skill, not verified automation for a public website. Never distribute .local, node_modules, browser profiles, cookies, credentials, or traces.
